title:
DashPass
In-store rewards
body:
Owned DashPass benefit awareness 
and discovery for In-store rewards
notes: Owned DashPass benefit awareness and surfacing benefits in discovery. Role moved from the original role slide to the cover.

title:
Membership Beyond
Just Delivery
notes: Brief DashPass benefits-home context, then In-Store Rewards. October 2026’s 2027 DashOS vision expands the ambition toward a trusted local decision guide. Keep this strategic context in the talk track, without adding a slide or implying the later vision resulted from this work.

title: Claim. Pay. Earn.
notes: Explain the product simply. Credit eligibility and timing depend on the offer. Show the high-level mechanism before the historical experience.

title: Where we started
notes: Original starting experience, using the three screens supplied by Vivian: Home → Landing → merchant detail.

title: Discovery Gaps
notes: Use research receipts for mental model, comprehension and personal relevance. These concise questions summarize the user-supplied problem; exact quotes remain in source material, not invented on slide.

title: What didn't work
notes: Existing source-native prototype screens: map-first, guided onboarding and first-visit $5 boost. These are design references; exact historical tested-variant equivalence remains unverified. All three entry tests were worse or unchanged overall per Vivian. Short reasons are design interpretations, not measured causal findings.

title:
The consumer
mental model
notes: The turning point is progressive disclosure and timing. First establish interest, then explain how at action, then show breadth and reasons to repeat. This is the exact three-part sequence in the user’s v4 outline.

title: How do I know?
notes: Section transition. Let the next three product moments answer the question through familiar browsing, the store, waiting for an order, and the Going Out sheet.

title: Meet them naturally
notes: Store slide. Start with a restaurant people recognize and connect delivery familiarity to an in-person reward. Shared USI source is journey context; its template menu and merchant details are fixtures. Demonstration uses Go Base October. Autoplay is an assembled walkthrough; the prototype remains interactive.

title: From benefit home
notes: Original supplied benefits recording, autoplaying and looping at source quality. Status bar normalized to 9:41 to match the deck.

title: Why should I care?
notes: Transition into familiarity and relevance.

title:
Catch attention
with familiarity
notes: Going Out sheet. Call out only a few elements: taller first-visit sheet, familiar merchant/food imagery, timely deals, National Favorites and prominent Claim. New-user vs returner preferences are directional user-supplied signals; shared prototype is not the exact experiment variant. Demonstration uses Go Base October. Autoplay is an assembled walkthrough; the prototype remains interactive.

title: How does it work?
notes: Section transition. Pause before the following demonstration.

title:
Explain after they
are interested
notes: Click Claim to open the explainer sheet, then go to the restaurant page. Show linked-card payment guidance at the moment someone has a reason to act. Vivian’s specific production contribution includes linked-card onboarding step 2. Shared journey controls remain interactive. Demonstration uses Go Base October. Autoplay is an assembled walkthrough; the prototype remains interactive.

title: Where can I use this?
notes: Section transition. Pause before the following demonstration.

title: Browse the options
notes: Expand the feed, scroll down a little, select Open now and Italian, then stop. Do not open a store.

title:
Celebrate and
reinforce
notes: Section transition. Next show the reward becoming tangible, then how collected signals can make future discovery more relevant.

title:
A more personal
next visit
notes: AI for You uses profile/context signals to make discovery more relevant. Discuss Vivian’s design contribution and collaboration with engineering on personalization and fine tuning; do not invent implementation details. Crop to the For You carousel because timer and DashPass colors were incidental screenshot artifacts. Review/feedback informing future discovery remains a proposal where launch is unverified.

title: What changed
notes: Program-level historical results from Going_Out_Q1_Review 2026: first-time conversion 0.7% Oct 6 to 2.2% Mar 9; returning conversion approximately 44–49% throughout Oct–Mar. These are historical program trends, not causal lift from this prototype or solely Vivian’s work. Claim rate and active order rate remain explicit TBD placeholders: available claim conversion lifts and active order conversion lifts are different metrics and were not substituted. Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1G8WpCGc2UBOSwnqtUVDO6gBrDCfAmUDwEGj40bxKf0k .
